[action] Built one self-contained HTML file: masthead (painter, years, Dutch; 1930; De Stijl), a live Three.js r170 canvas that redraws the described composition (large red square top right, small blue square bottom left, yellow rectangle bottom right, thick black lines on white) with a slow line drift, a CSS-grid fallback that shows until the module renders (so no-JS or CDN failure still shows the composition), four fact cards (Painter / Year / Movement / Why it matters), sections on the picture, Neoplasticism (six swatches: red, blue, yellow, white, grey, black) and De Stijl, a "Read more at the source" CTA, and a footer citing the Wikipedia source. Fonts: Archivo + IBM Plex Mono from Google Fonts; Three.js via importmap from the exact allowed CDN URL. Assumptions: the drawing is a plain geometric homage, labeled as such in the footer, not a reproduction; block proportions are my choice since the fact sheet gives no dimensions; `prefers-reduced-motion` renders the canvas statically.

Two revision rounds fixed a flipped canvas layout and a double-scaling camera bug; final reload is clean. All browser tabs closed (tab list now empty).

[next] Nothing required; if desired, real painting proportions could replace my stylized ones once a measured reference is allowed.
